name: Zeaxanthin
short: Only with lutein. AREDS2 (ages 50-85, risk of advanced macular degeneration): lung cancer up with beta carotene, not significantly with lutein/zeaxanthin. Deaths: may not change (very low certainty).
text: No safety study of zeaxanthin on its own was found; the main data come from the AREDS2 trial in 4203 people aged 50 to 85 at risk of advanced macular degeneration, who were randomised to lutein plus zeaxanthin, omega-3 fatty acids (DHA plus EPA), both, or placebo; all were also asked to take the original AREDS formula (vitamins C and E, beta carotene and zinc) or to accept randomisation to a variation of it. In the trial, more lung cancers occurred in the beta carotene group than in the no beta carotene group, mostly in former smokers, and the investigators suggested lutein plus zeaxanthin as a substitute carotenoid. In a 10-year follow-up of 3882 participants, the odds of lung cancer were 1.82 (95% CI 1.06 to 3.12) for those assigned beta carotene and 1.15 (95% CI 0.79 to 1.66), not statistically significant, for those assigned lutein/zeaxanthin. A Cochrane review found that lutein/zeaxanthin may have little or no effect on mortality (very low-certainty evidence) and noted that most studies were too small to detect rare adverse effects. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
